prompt: What is the reference angle for $150^\circ$? Give just the number of degrees.
hint: A reference angle is the acute angle between the terminal side and the $x$-axis — always measured to the nearest part of the $x$-axis.

hints.text: A reference angle is the acute angle between the terminal side and the $x$-axis — always measured to the nearest part of the $x$-axis.
$150^\circ$ is in Quadrant II, so measure back to the $180^\circ$ mark: $180 - 150$.

explanation: The terminal side of $150^\circ$ is in Quadrant II, leaning up and to the left.
The reference angle is how far it sits from the horizontal axis, which here is the $180^\circ$ direction.

alternativeExplanations.title: Mirror it into Quadrant I
steps: The reference angle is the Quadrant I twin of your angle — the same tilt, reflected.
$150^\circ$ leans $30^\circ$ above the leftward direction, which mirrors to $30^\circ$ above the rightward direction.
